subject: dwarfRifleman
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: dwarf rifleman with braided beard and blunderbuss.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
Looking at the helmet render, it sits too high above the head and the oversized thin brim makes it read like a floating pith hat rather than a proper dwarf helmet.

Eyes are nearly hidden beneath brow and mustache shading, so I should enlarge them and raise the brow line to give the face more presence.

For the arms, the left arm hangs limp while only the right hand grips the gun — it'd read better if the left hand supported the gun's fore-end instead, so I'm checking the gun's grip-to-muzzle axis to find a good support point along it.

Trying to reach that fore-end point from the left shoulder shows the distance exceeds the arm's length, so repositioning the gun closer to center doesn't quite solve the reach problem either. I'll keep the left arm relaxed at the side instead, since forcing it to the gun isn't geometrically feasible without bigger changes.

Checking the gun orientation in the three-quarter view — the stock reads correctly against the back and shoulder, and the barrel points forward at the hip, so that's fine. The beard, braids, and backpack bedroll all look acceptable, though the beard does cover the chest plate. The legs look very short and stubby, so I need to look at the knee guards next.

Looking closer at the knee guards, they're sitting too low on the thighs, almost like round eyes on the tabard sides — fine-ish placement though. Boots have thin dark sole slabs sticking out below, which read as separate plates, and the hips and pants blob look fine. The left arm's fingers point down thin, which is fine, and ground shadows aren't really a model concern.

The helmet brim looks too thin, and there's a problem with the head — too much bald skin dome visible between the brim and neck in the side view. I should add orange hair sweeping behind the head and down the sides, maybe styled as a ponytail, to cover that skin dome.

I'm also reconsidering the helmet height to balance covering the skull without clipping the brows or eyes, and I think I'll settle on a modest height while adding hair mass and sideburn tufts at the back of the head to fill in the bald look. Then I want to enlarge the eyes slightly, lift the brows a touch, and adjust the browridge geometry so it still reads naturally against the enlarged eyes.

I'm checking that the eye decals, browridge, and cheek blobs don't overlap and hide each other — lowering the browridge radius and raising its position, then pulling the cheek blobs further down so they don't cover the eye bottoms. The nose and helmet plume seem fine as is, maybe just reconsidering whether the plume looks too gnome-like versus a bolder dwarf crest, but I'll leave it. Shoulder spikes, pauldron, and bandolier all look acceptable, so now I'm thinking about what details might still be missing.

I want to give the left hand a more natural purpose by repositioning it to rest near the hip instead of the awkward splayed-out pose, checking it doesn't collide with the powder horn geometry. I'm also weighing small embellishments like a glowing muzzle ember or glowing rivets but deciding those are unnecessary since the lantern already provides glow. The crates and cannonballs in the scene are fine as background elements, and now I'm considering whether the helmet's dome could use more height or a ridge to feel more distinct.

Rather than adding a nose guard or cheek flaps, which risk colliding with the face, I decide to use the unused emblem texture as a decal on the helmet's front, calculating the dome's curvature and surface normal to figure out the right position, tilt, and size so it sits flush against the sloped surface without overlapping the goggles above it.

After the placement math gets messy, I abandon the helmet idea and consider other spots — the shoulder, backpack, chest boss — before settling on placing the emblem as a circular decal on the visible end-cap of the bedroll roll, applying it to both ends facing outward along the x-axis.

I'm also planning hair additions: a back-of-head cap blob sized to fit behind the skull without poking through the helmet, plus small sideburn tufts near the ears, while skipping a ponytail since it would clip the backpack geometry. Then I work out precise edits — nudging eye decal position/size outward so it doesn't overlap the nose blob, adjusting brow ridge and cheek blob coordinates slightly upward/inward, shifting the left-hand grip target, inserting the hair and sideburn blobs after the existing skull geometry, and appending the bedroll-emblem planes alongside the existing torus loop — before deciding to skip adding any glow effects to the gun and finalizing the edit list.
